_not.en: Cümle içinde duygu değişen okumalar (voice_gen.py inline). Etiketler yalnız sese gider; altyazı i18n/strings.csv'den.

D2_T_01.en: [groggy] [mumbling] ...Where am I? [confused] [rising panic] Why is everything sliding?

D2_H_02.tr: [worried] [over a crackling radio] Evlât! Ses geliyor mu? [hopeful] Vardın mı?
D2_H_02.en: [worried] [over a crackling radio] Son! Can you hear me? Did you get there?

D2_T_03.tr: [confused] Bir yokuştayım. [disgusted] Yokuş yağlı. [nervous] Arkamda... [pause] [terrified] bir gemi var.
D2_T_03.en: [confused] I'm on a hill. [disgusted] The hill is greased. [nervous] Behind me there's... [pause] [terrified] a ship.

D2_H_04.tr: [confused] Gemi mi? Yokuşta mı? [alarmed] [shouting] Evlât, 22 Nisan'dasın! Gemiler karadan yürütülüyor!
D2_H_04.en: [confused] A ship? On a hill? Son, it's the 22nd of April! They're hauling the ships overland!

D2_T_05.tr: [panicked] [out of breath] [shouting while running] Belgeselde bu kısım daha yavaştı!
D2_T_05.en: [panicked] [out of breath] [shouting while running] This bit was slower in the documentary!

D2_S_06.tr: [surprised] Hey! [angry] [shouting] Kızağın üstünde ne arıyorsun?! Çekil!
D2_S_06.en: [surprised] Oi! What are you doing on the slipway?! Move!

D2_H_WARRANTY.tr: [urgent] [shouting] Garanti bitiyor! [worried] Dönmek istersen şimdi bas!
D2_H_WARRANTY.en: [urgent] [shouting] The warranty's running out! [worried] If you want to come back, press it now!

D2_H_WARRANTY_END.en: [sighs] The warranty's expired. Now just run.

D2_H_AFTER_WARRANTY.tr: [flustered] Garanti bitti. [determined] Ben bir şey yapacağım, bekle.
D2_H_AFTER_WARRANTY.en: [flustered] The warranty's expired. I'll sort something out. Hang on.

D2_H_RADIO_YES.tr: [relieved] [exhales] Oh be. [warm] Sesini duymak güzel. [urgent] Şimdi koş.
D2_H_RADIO_YES.en: [relieved] [exhales] Oh, thank goodness. Good to hear you. Now run.

D2_T_STUMBLE_2.en: [panicked] [shouting] My fez! My fez fell off! [pause] [relieved] ...No, it's taped on.

D2_T_STUMBLE_2_NOFEZ.tr: [panicked] [shouting] Kravatım! Kravatım gitti! [pause] [relieved] ...Yok, yerinde. [sighs] [deadpan] Ben yerimde değilim.
D2_T_STUMBLE_2_NOFEZ.en: [panicked] [shouting] My tie! My tie's gone! [pause] [relieved] ...No, it's still there. [sighs] [deadpan] I'm the one who isn't.

D2_T_FALL.tr: [nervous] [out of breath] Yokuş bitiyor... [terrified] [shouting] Yokuş bitti!
D2_T_FALL.en: [nervous] [out of breath] The slope is ending... [terrified] [shouting] The slope has ended!

D2_T_08.tr: [gasps] [spluttering] Su! [shivering] Soğuk! [teeth chattering] [indignant] Nisan'da Haliç soğukmuş!
D2_T_08.en: [gasps] [spluttering] Water! [shivering] Cold! [teeth chattering] [indignant] The Golden Horn is cold in April!

D2_H_09.tr: [calm] [thinking] Yakında kıyı var [worried] ama askerler de var. [squinting] Uzakta bir zincir görüyorum... [pause] [sheepish] Yani sen görüyorsun.
D2_H_09.en: [calm] [thinking] There's a shore nearby, [worried] but there are soldiers too. [squinting] I can see a chain in the distance... [pause] [sheepish] Well, you can.

D2_T_CURRENT.en: [sheepish] I couldn't decide. [resigned] [sighs] The current decided for me.

D2_H_SWIM_HELP.tr: [reassuring] Evlât, akıntı seni taşıyor. [chuckles] Sen sadece çırpın, gerisini Haliç halleder.
D2_H_SWIM_HELP.en: [reassuring] Son, the current's got you. Just paddle, the Golden Horn will do the rest.

D2_H_SWIM_BOAT.tr: [alarmed] [urgent] Kayık geliyor! [instructing] Yaklaşınca CTRL, evlât, [shouting] dal!
D2_H_SWIM_BOAT.en: [alarmed] [urgent] Boat coming! When it's close, CTRL, son, dive!

D2_H_SWIM_BOAT_2.tr: [panicked] [shouting] Binme evlât, o devriye! [urgent] [hushed] Altından dal, görmesinler!
D2_H_SWIM_BOAT_2.en: [panicked] [shouting] Don't climb in, son, that's a patrol! Dive under, don't let them see you!

D2_T_SWIM_NOAIR.tr: [gasping for air] [panicked] Nefesim yok! [out of breath] Önce nefes, sonra dalış!
D2_T_SWIM_NOAIR.en: [gasping for air] [panicked] No breath left! [out of breath] Breathe first, dive later!

D2_T_AMPHORA.tr: [curious] Aşağıda bir amfora... [intrigued] Belki içinde şarap vardır. [hesitant] Belki de bin yıllık su. [firm] Açmıyorum.
D2_T_AMPHORA.en: [curious] An amphora down there... [intrigued] Maybe wine inside. [hesitant] Maybe thousand-year-old water. [firm] Not opening it.

D2_T_FEZ_FOUND.tr: [overjoyed] [shouting] Fesim! Beni buldu! [thoughtful] Ya da ben onu. [emotional] [sentimental] Haliç bizi birleştirdi.
D2_T_FEZ_FOUND.en: [overjoyed] [shouting] My fez! It found me! [thoughtful] Or I found it. [emotional] [sentimental] The Golden Horn reunited us.

D2_T_FEZ_SPARE.tr: [surprised] Yüzen bir fes. [pleased] Yedeğim oldu. [proud] [chuckles] Artık iki fesli bir adamım.
D2_T_FEZ_SPARE.en: [surprised] A floating fez. [pleased] Now I have a spare. [proud] [chuckles] I am a man of two fezzes.

D2_T_10.tr: [out of breath] [whispers] Kimse görmedi. [relieved] Harika. [curious] Şimdi... burası pazar yeri mi?
D2_T_10.en: [out of breath] [whispers] Nobody saw me. [relieved] Brilliant. [curious] Now... is this a market?

D2_HA_11.tr: [suspicious] [squinting] Az önce yokuştan bir fes kaymadı mı?
D2_HA_11.en: [suspicious] [squinting] Didn't a fez just slide down that hill?

D2_HA_11_NOFEZ.tr: [suspicious] Az önce yokuştan biri kaymadı mı? [puzzled] Redingotlu biri?
D2_HA_11_NOFEZ.en: [suspicious] Didn't someone just slide down that hill? [puzzled] Someone in a frock coat?

D2_S_14_NOFEZ.tr: [alarmed] [shouting] Yakalayın! [baffled] Deli mi bu, casus mu?!
D2_S_14_NOFEZ.en: [alarmed] [shouting] Seize him! [baffled] Is he mad or a spy?!

D2_T_15.en: [panicked] [pleading] I'm not a spy, [desperate] [shouting] I'm in insurance!

D2_H_17.en: [sheepish] [apologetic] We didn't have the budget for this scene, son.

D2_H_19.tr: [calm] [instructing] Şehir tarafına yürü. Zincirin üstünde. [cautious] Dengeni koru.
D2_H_19.en: [calm] [instructing] Walk to the city side. On the chain. Keep your balance.

D2_T_22.en: [yelps] I slipped. [outraged] [shouting] Is the chain greased too?!

D2_T_ARROW_1.tr: [terrified] [shouting] Bir ok! Bana ok attılar! [indignant] Sigortacıya ok atılır mı?!
D2_T_ARROW_1.en: [terrified] [shouting] An arrow! They shot an arrow at me! [indignant] Who shoots an insurance agent?!

D2_T_ARROW_2.en: [shocked] It grazed the fez! [pause] [impressed] Turns out the fez is armour.

D2_T_ARROW_2_NOFEZ.tr: [shocked] Saçımı sıyırdı! [shaky] Fes başımda olsaydı fes giderdi.
D2_T_ARROW_2_NOFEZ.en: [shocked] It grazed my hair! [shaky] If I'd had the fez on, the fez would be gone.

D2_T_ARROW_3.tr: [nervous laugh] Uyarı atışı herhalde. [shaky] [sarcastic] Çok başarılı bir uyarı.
D2_T_ARROW_3.en: [nervous laugh] A warning shot, I guess. [shaky] [sarcastic] A very effective warning.

D2_H_24.tr: [disappointed] O kadar mı? [sighs] [wounded pride] Makineyi kırk yılda yaptım.
D2_H_24.en: [disappointed] That's it? [sighs] [wounded pride] I spent forty years building that machine.

D2_T_25.tr: [out of breath] Hikmet Amca, beni duyuyor musun? [pause] [awed] [quietly] Ben... gerçekten 1453'teyim.
D2_T_25.en: [out of breath] Hikmet, can you hear me? [pause] [awed] [quietly] I'm... actually in 1453.

D3_N_RESIST.tr: [alarmed] [shouting] Makine direniyor! Tavuk! Bir ok! [composing himself] [stiff] ...Mühür basılı tutulur. [bureaucratic] Yönetmelik öyle.

D3_H_RESIST.tr: [nervous] [hurried] O tavuk bizim değil! [pause] ...O ok da bizim değil. [innocent] Ben hiçbir şeyi tanımıyorum.

D1P_T_01.tr: [sleepy] Mmh... Alo? Gecenin bu saatinde... [alarmed] kim öldü?

D1P_H_02.tr: [cheerful] Kimse ölmedi evlâdım, ağzından yel alsın. [mischievous] Henüz. Uyuyor muydun?
D1P_H_02.en: [cheerful] Nobody died, son. [mischievous] Yet. [innocent] Were you asleep?

D1P_T_03.tr: [sleepy] [annoyed] Saat gecenin üçü Hikmet Amca. Tabii ki uyuyordum!
D1P_T_03.en: [sleepy] [annoyed] It's three in the morning, Hikmet. [sighs] Of course I was asleep.

D1P_H_04.tr: [pleased] Güzel, demek dinlendin. [excited] Hadi, fırla hemen garaja gel!
D1P_H_04.en: [pleased] Good, so you're rested. [excited] [urgent] Come to the garage. Now!

D1P_T_05.tr: [sleepy] [pleading] Sabah konuşsak olmaz mı? Dokuzda poliçe toplantım var...
D1P_T_05.en: [sleepy] [pleading] Can't it wait till morning? [whiny] I've got a policy meeting at nine...

D1P_H_06.tr: [philosophical] Sabah dokuz... Ne kadar da göreceli bir kavram. [firm] Beş dakikan var evlât.
D1P_H_06.en: [philosophical] Nine in the morning... Such a relative concept. [firm] You have five minutes.

D1P_T_07.tr: [sleepy] [mumbling] O zaman beş dakika daha kestiririm...
D1P_T_07.en: [sleepy] [mumbling] Then I'll sleep five more minutes... [yawning]

D1P_H_08.en: [shouting from the street] [loud] TOLGAAA! [annoyed] And bring my slipper back!

D1P_T_09.tr: [startled] Tamam, tamam, geliyorum! [grumbling] Dur bari kravatımı takayım...
D1P_T_09.en: [startled] [flustered] Okay, okay! I'm coming! [grumbling] [hurried] Let me at least put on a tie...

D1P_T_10.tr: [deadpan] Gecenin üçünde terlikle davet. Klasik Hikmet Amca.
D1P_T_10.en: [deadpan] [sighs] An invitation by slipper. [wry] Classic Hikmet.

D1_T_03.tr: [tired] Hikmet Amca, gözünü seveyim, bu saatte... Ne bu şimdi?
D1_T_03.en: [tired] [grumpy] Hikmet, it's three in the morning. [confused] What is this?

D1_H_01.tr: [warm] Evlâdım, hele bir yaklaş, şuna bak. [excited] Bu sefer büyük bir buluş yaptım!
D1_H_01.en: [warm] Son, come and look at this. [proud] [excited] I've made a great discovery.

D1_H_02.tr: [casual] Şimdi bunu deneyecek gözü kara biri lazım. [sly] Tercihen sigortalı.
D1_H_02.en: [casual] I need someone to test it. [pause] [sly] Preferably someone insured.

D1_H_06.tr: [serious] Makinenin tek bir arızası var evlât: [baffled] çalışıyor. Açıkçası ben de beklemiyordum.
D1_H_06.en: [serious] There's only one problem with it: [pause] [baffled] it works. I never expected that.

D1_T_05.tr: [skeptical] Dur dur dur. Şaka yapıyorsun, değil mi? [whispers] Bu gerçekten çalışıyor mu?
D1_T_05.en: [skeptical] Wait, wait, wait. You're joking, right? [whispers] Does this thing actually work?

D1_T_07.tr: [slowly realising] Dur bir dakika... [excited] Yani ben bu kafayla gerçekten 1453'e gidebilir miyim?
D1_T_07.en: [slowly realising] Wait. [growing excitement] Could I go to 1453? With everything I know now? [excited] I've watched twenty documentaries!

D1_H_07B.en: [shrugs] Of course, son. [mildly impatient] I told you, the machine works.

D1_T_07C.tr: [boastful] Hikmet Amca, ben 1453 üstüne kaç tane belgesel izledim, haberin var mı?
D1_T_07C.en: [excited] [boastful] Do you know how many documentaries I've watched about 1453?

D1_H_08.tr: [placating] Gitmesine gidersin de... [skeptical] o kıyafetle mi?
D1_H_08.en: [placating] You could. [skeptical] [looking him up and down] In those clothes?

D1_T_09.tr: [reluctant] Haklısın, dönem kıyafeti lazım... [excited] Dur! Şirketin 'Osmanlı Gecesi'nden kalan kostüm hâlâ bende!
D1_T_09.en: [reluctant] You're right. I need period clothing... [sudden idea] [excited] Wait! I've still got the costume from the office's Ottoman Night party!

D1_H_10.tr: [blunt] Hiç yakışmadı evlât. [chuckles] Ama kim bilir, belki orada moda olur.
D1_H_10.en: [blunt] Doesn't suit you at all. [chuckles] But who knows, it might be in fashion there.

D1_T_11.tr: [offended] Ama kostümcü 'abi, tam dönem işi' dedi.
D1_T_11.en: [defensive] [offended] The costume shop said it was 'totally period'.

D1_H_12.tr: [dry] İyi de, hangi dönem olduğunu söyledi mi?

D1_T_MIRROR.tr: [looking in the mirror] Ceket, saçlar dağınık. [wry] Hikmet Amca'nın 'o kıyafetle mi?' sorusu bence haksız değildi.
D1_T_MIRROR.en: [looking in the mirror] Jacket, hair all over the place. [wry] Uncle Hikmet's 'in those clothes?' wasn't an unfair question.

D1_T_MIRROR_FEZ.tr: [pleased] Fes de yakıştı ha. [hesitant] Biraz. Yarım yamalak... [sighs] Tamam, yakışmadı. [stubborn] Ama dönemsel!
D1_T_MIRROR_FEZ.en: [pleased] The fez suits me too. [hesitant] Sort of. Halfway... [sighs] [resigned] Fine, it doesn't. [stubborn] But it's period!

D1_H_13.tr: [businesslike] Şimdi çanta. Etrafta işe yarar ne varsa al. [warning] Ama beşten fazlası sığmaz.
D1_H_13.en: [businesslike] Now, the bag. Take anything useful. [warning] But it won't fit more than five.

D1_H_14.tr: [serious] Beşten fazla sığmaz. Ben denedim, dikişleri patladı. Koli bandı ondan.
D1_H_14.en: [serious] It won't take more than five. I tried. [grim] The bag exploded. [matter-of-fact] That's why there's duct tape.

D1_H_16.tr: [proud] Bak: bu taraf telsiz, bu taraf kumanda. Koli bandıyla birleştirdim.
D1_H_16.en: [proud] This is a radio. This is a remote. [very proud] I've taped them together.

D1_H_17.tr: [salesman voice] Kırmızı düğme acil dönüş. Baktın pabuç pahalı, ilk 10 dakika koşulsuz iade garantisi var.
D1_H_17.en: [salesman voice] The red button is the emergency return. [cheerful] If things get too hot, there's a no-questions-asked refund for the first ten minutes.

D1_H_18.tr: [uncertain] Öbür düğmeler... salondaki televizyonun kanalını değiştiriyor olabilir.
D1_H_18.en: [uncertain] The other buttons... [shrugs] might change the channel.

D1_H_19.tr: [stern] Bir de: o kırmızı düğmeye sakın basma. [deadly serious] Ciddiyim.
D1_H_19.en: [stern] And one more thing: don't press the red button. [deadly serious] I mean it.

D1_T_20.tr: [confused] İyi de, az önce 'acil dönüş' demedin mi?
D1_T_20.en: [confused] You just said it was the emergency return.

D1_H_21.tr: [as if it's obvious] Acil olursa bas, acil değilse basma. Bu kadar basit evlât.
D1_H_21.en: [patient] [as if it's obvious] Press it if it's an emergency. Don't if it isn't. [satisfied] Simple.

D1_H_22.en: [encouraging] Go on. Type the year on the panel.

D1_H_23.tr: [reading slowly] On dört elli üç... [puzzled] Saat mi kurdun evlât?
D1_H_23.en: [reading slowly] Fourteen fifty-three... [puzzled] Did you type a time, son?

D1_T_24.tr: [exasperated] Ne saati Hikmet Amca, bin dört yüz elli üç yazdım!
D1_T_24.en: [frustrated] [exasperated] I typed fourteen fifty-three! The year!

D1_H_25.tr: [unbothered] Makine saat diye okudu. Neyse, rakam rakamdır. [cheerful] Hadi, çık platforma.
D1_H_25.en: [unbothered] That's how the machine read it. [shrugs] Never mind, a time's a time. [cheerful] Get on the platform.

D1_H_YEAR_2026.tr: [amused] Zaten 2026'dayız evlât. Garajdan garaja mı gideceksin?
D1_H_YEAR_2026.en: [amused] We're already in 2026, son. Going from the garage to the garage, are we?

D1_T_YEAR_OTHER.en: [flustered] No, no. [muttering] It was supposed to be 1453.

D1_H_26.tr: [alarmed] Hay Allah, takıldı! [urgent] Bir tekme lazım!
D1_H_26.en: [alarmed] [shouting] It's stuck! [urgent] It needs a kick!

D1_H_KICK_WEAK.tr: [mocking] Bu tekme mi? Komşunun kapısını çalıyorsun sanki. [shouting] Bir daha!
D1_H_KICK_WEAK.en: [mocking] Call that a kick? You're knocking on a door. [shouting] Again!

D1_H_KICK_WEAK2.tr: [fired up] Bacağınla değil, öfkenle vur evlât! [wistful] 1977'deki düğünde benim yapamadığımı sen yap!
D1_H_KICK_WEAK2.en: [fired up] [shouting] Not with your leg, son, with your rage! [wistful] Do what I couldn't do at that wedding in 1977!

D1_H_KICK_STRONG.tr: [panicked] Yavaş evlât! [wincing] O panelin garantisi yok!
D1_H_KICK_STRONG.en: [panicked] [shouting] Easy! [wincing] That panel has no warranty!

D1_T_28.en: [pained] [shouting] Ow! My foot! [whimpering] My toes are gone!

D1_H_27.tr: [satisfied] Hah şöyle! Bu meret hep böyle çalışır.

D1_H_29.tr: [sighs] Paneli çatlattın evlât. [surprised] Ama bak, telsizin sinyali bir çentik arttı... Çatlak anten olmuş. [unbothered] Neyse, iki tur bant çekeriz.
D1_H_29.en: [sighs] You cracked the panel, son. [surprised] But look, your radio signal went up a notch... the crack must be acting as an aerial. [unbothered] Never mind, we'll give it two rounds of tape.

D1_H_30.tr: [shouting over machine noise] Padişah'a benden selam söyle! [curious] Bir de sor bakalım, o toplar kaç volt?
D1_H_30.en: [shouting over machine noise] [cheerful] Say hello to the Sultan for me! [curious] And ask him how many volts those cannons are!

D1_H_31.tr: [puzzled] Yahu daha bir yere gitmedin ki! [suspicious] Nereden döndün?
D1_H_31.en: [puzzled] You haven't even left. [suspicious] Where did you come back from?

D1_H_DEMO_1.tr: [showman] Dur, gözünle gör. [playful] Şu terliği bir dakikalığına yolluyorum.
D1_H_DEMO_1.en: [showman] Here, let me show you. [playful] I'm sending my slipper off for a minute.

D1_H_DEMO_2.en: [pause] [surprised] ...It's back. [pause] [stunned] [quietly] There's an arrow in it.

D1_T_DEMO_3.tr: [panicked] Bu gerçek ok Hikmet Amca! Tüyleri bile var! [worried] Nereye gitti bu terlik?!
D1_T_DEMO_3.en: [panicked] [shouting] That arrow's real! [disbelief] It's even got feathers! [worried] Where did that slipper go?

D1_H_DEMO_4.tr: [sheepish] Kadranda 1453 yazıyormuş evlât. Ben de şimdi fark ettim.
D1_H_DEMO_4.en: [sheepish] The dial said 1453. [embarrassed] I've only just noticed.

D1_H_IDLE_1.tr: [warning] Makineye çok sokulma evlât, statik yapıyor, saçını çeker.
D1_H_IDLE_1.en: [warning] [casual] Don't stand too close to the machine. It pulls your hair.

D1_H_IDLE_2.tr: [casual] Çerçeveye mi baktın? Boş o. [mysterious] Şimdilik.
D1_H_IDLE_2.en: [casual] That frame? It's empty. [mysterious] For now.

D1_H_IDLE_3.tr: [casual] Duvardaki takvim mi? [wistful] 1977'den kalma. Koparmaya elim varmadı.
D1_H_IDLE_3.en: [casual] The calendar? [wistful] [quiet] 1977. I could never bring myself to tear it off.

D1_H_IDLE_4.tr: [amused] Fes kaşındırıyor mu? [mock serious] Katlanacaksın evlât, dönem otantikliği.
D1_H_IDLE_4.en: [amused] Is the fez itchy? [mock serious] That's period authenticity, son.

D12_F_EDIRNE.tr: [thoughtful] [slowly] Seni bir havuzdan hatırlıyor gibiyim… [dismissive] Neyse. Devam et.
D12_F_EDIRNE.en: [thoughtful] [slowly] I feel I remember you from a pool… [dismissive] Never mind. Go on.

D14_N_SICIL_EDIRNE_KEBAB.tr: [dry] Bir de 1444 var: kalibrasyon atlaması. [deadpan] Raporda 'kebap' kelimesi geçen tek dosya sizinki.
D14_N_SICIL_EDIRNE_KEBAB.en: [dry] And then there's 1444: the calibration jump. [deadpan] Yours is the only file in the archive containing the word 'kebab'.

D14_N_SICIL_EDIRNE_LEGEND.tr: [dry] Bir de 1444 var. [sighs] Drakula'nın telif hakkı… [deadpan] Büro'nun avukatları inceliyor.
D14_N_SICIL_EDIRNE_LEGEND.en: [dry] And then there's 1444. [sighs] The rights to Dracula… [deadpan] the Bureau's lawyers are looking into it.

D14_N_SICIL_EDIRNE_NONE.tr: [dry] Bir de 1444 var. Bir karikatür. [softly] [slight smile] Sicile işlemedim; çok benzemişsiniz.
D14_N_SICIL_EDIRNE_NONE.en: [dry] And then there's 1444. A caricature. [softly] [slight smile] I left it off the record; it's a good likeness.

D14_N_SICIL_EDIRNE_POLICY.tr: [dry] Bir de 1444 var. Eflak'ta bir sigorta şirketi kurdurmuşsunuz. [deadpan] Merkez sizden komisyon istiyor.
D14_N_SICIL_EDIRNE_POLICY.en: [dry] And then there's 1444. You got an insurance company founded in Wallachia. [deadpan] Head office wants your commission.

D17E_G_01.tr: [stern] Mehmed. Otur. [dry] Misafir de otursun; [wise] ayakta alınan ilim ayakta kalır.
D17E_G_01.en: [stern] Mehmed. Sit. [dry] The guest too; [wise] knowledge taken standing stays standing.

D17E_G_02.tr: [stern] [testing] Dünkü sual: âlem kadîm midir, hâdis mi?
D17E_G_02.en: [stern] [testing] Yesterday's question: is the world eternal, or created in time?

D17E_G_03.tr: [dry] [unimpressed] Sultan gibi konuştun. [firm] Şimdi talebe gibi otur.
D17E_G_03.en: [dry] [unimpressed] You spoke like a sultan. [firm] Now sit like a student.

D17E_G_04.en: [stern] Guest. [pause] [probing] You tell me: what shape is the world?

D17E_G_DODGE.tr: [grudgingly impressed] Çevik. [cold] Ama cahil. [dry] Çevik cahil daha tehlikelidir.
D17E_G_DODGE.en: [grudgingly impressed] Quick. [cold] But ignorant. [dry] A quick ignoramus is the more dangerous kind.

D17E_G_DUNNO.tr: [approving] [slowly] Bilmiyorum demek ilmin yarısıdır. [dry] [slight chuckle] Yarısını bilen misafirden korkmam.
D17E_G_DUNNO.en: [approving] [slowly] Saying 'I don't know' is half of knowledge. [dry] [slight chuckle] I don't fear a guest who knows half.

D17E_G_END.tr: [firm] Yeter. Mehmed, kütüphaneye. İskender'ini al; [annoyed] misafiri de götür, minderimi ıslatıyor.
D17E_G_END.en: [firm] Enough. Mehmed, to the library. Take your Alexander; [annoyed] and take the guest, he's dripping on my cushion.

D17E_G_ROUND.tr: [dismissive] Fotoğraf nedir bilmem. [proudly] Ama Batlamyus küre der; Bîrûnî bir dağın tepesinden ölçtü bile.
D17E_G_ROUND.en: [dismissive] I don't know what a photo is. [proudly] But Ptolemy says a sphere; al-Biruni even measured it from a mountaintop.

D17E_G_ROUND_2.tr: [patient] Ufkun eğiminden. Ders bitince anlatırım. [stern] Önce Kur'an.
D17E_G_ROUND_2.en: [patient] From the dip of the horizon. I'll explain after the lesson. [stern] Quran first.

D17E_G_SHOES.tr: [stern] Pabuçlar basamakta kalır, misafir. [wise] Toz da, kibir de eşikte silkelenir.
D17E_G_SHOES.en: [stern] Shoes stay on the step, guest. [wise] Dust and pride are both shaken off at the threshold.

D17E_H_DIVAN.tr: [urgent] [out of breath] Sultanım! Divan toplandı, sizi bekliyor!
D17E_H_DIVAN.en: [urgent] [out of breath] My Sultan! The council has assembled and awaits you!

D17E_H_DIVAN_2.tr: [forced politeness] Elbette, Sultanım. [through gritted teeth] Divan… sizi bekleyedursun.
D17E_H_DIVAN_2.en: [forced politeness] Of course, my Sultan. [through gritted teeth] The council will… wait for you.

D17E_H_SPY.tr: [alarmed] [shouting] Sarayda yabancı! Frenk casusu! Tutun şunu!
D17E_H_SPY.en: [alarmed] [shouting] A stranger in the palace! A Frankish spy! Seize him!

D17E_H_TOSS.en: [commanding] [smug] Throw the spy in the pool! [mocking] Let him cool off!

D17E_MU_01.tr: [urgent] [out of breath] Nihat Bey! Eflak masası arıyor! [alarmed] Vikipedi'de bir şey değişti!
D17E_MU_01.en: [urgent] [out of breath] Mr Nihat! The Wallachia desk is calling! [alarmed] Something's changed on Wikipedia!

D17E_M_01.tr: [curious] Sen sudan çıktın! İskender'in hikâyesinde de sudan çıkan biri var: ölümsüzlük suyunu bulan.
D17E_M_01.en: [curious] You came out of the water! In Alexander's story someone comes out of the water too: the one who found the water of life.

D17E_M_03.tr: [thoughtful] Filozoflar 'âlem hep vardı' der, Gazâlî 'sonradan yaratıldı' der. Ben ikisini de dinlerim, sonra kendim karar veririm.
D17E_M_03.en: [thoughtful] The philosophers say the world always existed; al-Ghazali says it was created. I listen to both, then I make up my own mind.

D17E_M_AVLU.tr: [matter-of-fact] İşte arkadaşlarım: Vlad ve küçük kardeşi Radu.
D17E_M_AVLU.en: [matter-of-fact] Here are my friends: Vlad and his little brother Radu.

D17E_M_BOOK.en: [firm] I don't read my fate from a book. I write it.

D17E_M_BYE_TIME.en: [shouting] [laughing] See you in Constantinople, lift man!

D17E_M_COME.tr: [brisk] Hadi gel, ders vakti. Hocam misafiri sever; ama değneğini daha çok sever.
D17E_M_COME.en: [brisk] Come on, it's lesson time. My teacher likes guests; but he likes his rod even more.

D17E_M_CUBE.tr: [curious] Çantandaki o renkli şey ne? Bir bilmece mi?
D17E_M_CUBE.en: [curious] What's that colourful thing in your bag? A riddle?

D17E_M_CUBE_2.tr: [casual] Önce köşeleri alırsın. Merkez kendiliğinden düşer.
D17E_M_CUBE_2.en: [casual] First you take the corners. The centre falls by itself.

D17E_M_DIVAN.tr: [cool] Divan beni beklemiyor ki, Halil Paşa'yı bekliyor. Ben de dersimi bekliyorum.
D17E_M_DIVAN.en: [cool] The council isn't waiting for me, it's waiting for Halil Pasha. And I'm waiting for my lesson.

D17E_M_DRACUL.tr: [lowered voice] Babalarının adı Dracul: ejderha. Ejderha Tarikatı'nın şövalyesi.
D17E_M_DRACUL.en: [lowered voice] Their father is called Dracul: the dragon. A knight of the Order of the Dragon.

D17E_M_DUNNO.tr: [writing] Yazdım. 'Bilmiyorum' diyebilen ödülü hak eder. Bir gün ben de böylelerini ödüllendireceğim.
D17E_M_DUNNO.en: [writing] Noted. Anyone who can say 'I don't know' deserves a reward. One day I'll reward people like that.

D17E_M_FLAT.tr: [incredulous] Düz mü? Batlamyus'u okumadın mı? Bîrûnî ölçtü!
D17E_M_FLAT.en: [incredulous] Flat? Haven't you read Ptolemy? Al-Biruni measured it!

D17E_M_GREEK_2.tr: [amused] Rumcan benim kedimden kötü. Ama yüzün dürüst. Islak ama dürüst.
D17E_M_GREEK_2.en: [amused] Your Greek is worse than my cat's. But you have an honest face. Wet, but honest.

D17E_M_HIZIR.tr: [impressed] Hızır ölümsüzdür. Hocamın değneği de ölümsüz. Bakalım hangisi daha dayanıklı.
D17E_M_HIZIR.en: [impressed] Hızır is immortal. So is my teacher's rod. Let's see which one lasts longer.

D17E_M_ISK.tr: [proudly] Bu, Ahmedî'nin İskendernâme'si. İskender'in hocası Aristo'ydu; benimki de Molla Gürânî.
D17E_M_ISK.en: [proudly] This is Ahmedi's Book of Alexander. Alexander's teacher was Aristotle; mine is Molla Gurani.

D17E_M_ISK_2.tr: [deadpan] Kullanmazdı herhalde. O yüzden İskender Hindistan'da durdu.
D17E_M_ISK_2.en: [deadpan] Probably not. That's why Alexander stopped at India.

D17E_M_KAYSER.tr: [curious] Rum'un hükümdarına Kayser derler. Peki bu ad ilk kimin adıydı, biliyor musun?
D17E_M_KAYSER.en: [curious] They call the ruler of Rum 'Kayser'. So whose name was it first? Do you know?

D17E_M_KEB.tr: [chewing] Şişte et! Bunu ordu da yesin; seferde kazan taşımaktan iyidir.
D17E_M_KEB.en: [chewing] Meat on a skewer! The army should eat this; it beats hauling cauldrons on campaign.

D17E_M_NAME.tr: [formal] Ben Mehmed. Babam tahtı bana bırakıp Manisa'ya çekildi. Taht çok büyük, oturunca ayaklarım yere değmiyor.
D17E_M_NAME.en: [formal] I'm Mehmed. My father left me the throne and went off to Manisa. The throne is huge; when I sit on it my feet don't reach the floor.

D17E_M_NOTE.tr: [shy] Bu benim defterim. Tuğra çalışıyorum. Şu da Kostantiniyye: surları, zinciri… Kızıl Elma.
D17E_M_NOTE.en: [shy] This is my notebook. I'm practising my tughra. And that's Constantinople: its walls, its chain… the Red Apple.

D17E_M_NOTE_2.tr: [shy] Şiir de yazıyorum. Mahlasım Avnî, yani 'yardım eden'. Gerçi daha kimseye yardım etmedim.
D17E_M_NOTE_2.en: [shy] I write poems too. My pen name is Avni, it means 'the one who helps'. Though I haven't helped anyone yet.

D17E_M_POL.tr: [lowered voice] Bunu Halil Paşa duymasın; vergisini koyar.
D17E_M_POL.en: [lowered voice] Don't let Halil Pasha hear of this; he'll tax it.

D17E_M_ROD.tr: [conspiratorial] Babam hocama bir değnek verdi, 'söz dinlemezse vur' diye. İlk gün güldüm.
D17E_M_ROD.en: [conspiratorial] My father gave my teacher a rod and said, 'If he won't listen, hit him.' On the first day I laughed.

D17E_M_ROD_2.tr: [rueful] Sonra gülmedim. Kur'an'ı da çabucak hatmettim.
D17E_M_ROD_2.en: [rueful] Then I stopped laughing. And I finished the Quran very quickly.

D17E_M_RUN_GREEK.en: [shouting] Sirtaki! The pool! Back where you came from!

D17E_M_RUN_HIZIR.en: [shouting] Hızır! The pool! Back where you came from!

D17E_M_RUN_TIME.en: [shouting] Lift man! The pool! Back where you came from!

D17E_M_SALAD.tr: [puzzled] Kayser'in salatası mı? Rum hükümdarları ot mu yerdi?
D17E_M_SALAD.en: [puzzled] The Caesar's salad? Did the rulers of Rum graze on greens?

D17E_M_SELFIE.tr: [skeptical] Sopayla resim mi yapılır? Ressamlar fırça kullanır.
D17E_M_SELFIE.en: [skeptical] A picture with a stick? Painters use brushes.

D17E_M_SELFIE_2.en: [playful] [giggles] I'll draw you too. Stick and all.

D17E_M_STARS.tr: [excited] Bu bir usturlap. Semerkand'da Uluğ Bey bütün göğü bir kitaba yazdı: bin yıldız, bin satır.
D17E_M_STARS.en: [excited] This is an astrolabe. In Samarkand, Ulugh Beg wrote the whole sky into a book: a thousand stars, a thousand lines.

D17E_M_STARS_2.tr: [determined] Bir gün onun öğrencilerini buraya çağıracağım. Gelsinler, yıldızları bizim şehrimizde saysınlar.
D17E_M_STARS_2.en: [determined] One day I'll invite his students here. Let them come and count the stars in our city.

D17E_M_TELL_2.tr: [solemn] Peygamber haber verdi: 'Kostantiniyye mutlaka fethedilecek; onu fetheden komutan ne güzel komutandır.' O komutan ben olacağım. Yaşını bilmiyordum; sağ ol.
D17E_M_TELL_2.en: [solemn] The Prophet foretold it: 'Constantinople will surely be conquered; how excellent the commander who conquers it.' I will be that commander. I didn't know the age; thank you.

D17E_M_TIME.tr: [intrigued] Aristo, zaman hareketin sayısıdır der. Sen hangi hareketle geldin?
D17E_M_TIME.en: [intrigued] Aristotle says time is the number of motion. So which motion brought you here?

D17E_M_TIME_2.en: [writing] Lift. Noted. I'll ask my teacher for the Arabic.

D17E_M_TO_AVLU.tr: [eager] Gel, seni arkadaşlarımla tanıştıracağım. Biri çok ilginçtir.
D17E_M_TO_AVLU.en: [eager] Come, I'll introduce you to my friends. One of them is very interesting.

D17E_M_VENI.tr: [impressed] Üç kelime! Koca bir zaferi üç kelimeye sığdırmış. Ben bir şehre girdiğimde bir beyit okuyacağım.
D17E_M_VENI.en: [impressed] Three words! He fit a whole victory into three words. When I enter a city, I'll recite a couplet.

D17E_M_VLAD.tr: [firm] Rehine kesilmez, okutulur. Sen de mantık dersine gel; kavgayı sopayla değil, sözle kazanırsın.
D17E_M_VLAD.en: [firm] Hostages aren't killed, they're taught. Come to logic class too; you win fights with words, not sticks.

D17E_N_BACK_1.tr: [exasperated] [through gritted teeth] Beş dakika dedim. Kalibrasyon dedim. [sighs] Boş tarla dedim.
D17E_N_BACK_1.en: [exasperated] [through gritted teeth] I said five minutes. I said calibration. [sighs] I said an empty field.

D17E_N_CAL_1.tr: [matter-of-fact] Kamera tamam. Şimdi makineyi kameraya alıştıralım: beş dakikalık bir kalibrasyon atlaması. [reassuring] 1453, boş bir tarla. Kimse görmez.
D17E_N_CAL_1.en: [matter-of-fact] The camera's fine. Now we get the machine used to it: a five-minute calibration jump. [reassuring] 1453, an empty field. Nobody will see you.

D17E_N_FIX.tr: [stamping paper] [dry] Düzeltme formu. Z-1444/K. [satisfied] Tarih inatçıdır; dosya kapanır.
D17E_N_FIX.en: [stamping paper] [dry] Correction form. Z-1444/K. [satisfied] History is stubborn; the file is closed.

D17E_N_FIX_2.tr: [weary] Tarih inatçıdır, Tolga Bey. [deadpan] Dipnotlar daha da inatçı.
D17E_N_FIX_2.en: [weary] History is stubborn, Mr Tolga. [deadpan] Footnotes are more stubborn still.

D17E_N_LEB.tr: [suspicious] O ses neydi? Kadranın dişlisine bir şey mi kaçtı? [alarmed] Leblebi mi o?!
D17E_N_LEB.en: [suspicious] What was that noise? Did something get into the dial's gears? [alarmed] Is that a chickpea?!

D17E_N_LIFT_1.tr: [formal] [dry] Kabine girin. Kapı kapanınca kıpırdamayın; makine kıpırtı sevmez.
D17E_N_LIFT_1.en: [formal] [dry] Step into the cabin. Once the door shuts, don't fidget; the machine hates fidgeting.

D17E_N_META.tr: [strained calm] Tolga Bey. Bu oyunun adı 'Gerçek Tarih Bu Değil', farkındayım. [rising anger] Ama bu bir isim, görev tanımı değil! [shouting] Ne yaptın sen?!
D17E_N_META.en: [strained calm] Mr Tolga. I'm aware this game is called 'Not a History Game'. [rising anger] But that's a title, not a job description! [shouting] What have you done?!

D17E_N_META_2.en: [embarrassed] [composing himself] …Nothing. I beg your pardon. [formal] What have you done, sir?

D17E_N_NO.tr: [panicked] Hayır hayır hayır… [shouting] Bin dört yüz kırk dört değil! Tutunun!
D17E_N_NO.en: [panicked] No, no, no… [shouting] Not fourteen forty-four! Hold on!

D17E_N_PHONE.tr: [alarmed] Kapatın! 2026'dan gelen sinyal kadranı bozar… [shouting] Kapatın şunu!
D17E_N_PHONE.en: [alarmed] Hang up! A signal from 2026 will throw the dial… [shouting] Hang it up!

D17E_N_PULL.tr: [over a crackling radio] [urgent] Tolga Bey! Sinyaliniz 1444'ten geliyor! [strained] Tutunun, çekiyorum!
D17E_N_PULL.en: [over a crackling radio] [urgent] Mr Tolga! Your signal's coming from 1444! [strained] Hold on, I'm pulling you out!

D17E_N_SALAD.tr: [over a crackling radio] [exasperated] Salatayı tarihe sokmayın!
D17E_N_SALAD.en: [over a crackling radio] [exasperated] Keep the salad out of history!

D17E_N_TOWEL.tr: [deadpan] Peştemal. Büro'nun malı; demirbaşa kayıtlı. [stern] İade edilecek.
D17E_N_TOWEL.en: [deadpan] A peshtemal. Bureau property, on the inventory. [stern] It will be returned.

D17E_N_WHAT_KEBAB.tr: [dry] Ormanı kebaba çevirmişsiniz. [deadpan] Romanya her yaz festival yapıyor. [sighs] Afişte sizin bıyığınız var.
D17E_N_WHAT_KEBAB.en: [dry] You turned the forest into kebab. [deadpan] Romania holds a festival every summer. [sighs] Your moustache is on the poster.

D17E_N_WHAT_LEGEND.tr: [dry] Drakula'yı siz uydurmuşsunuz. [deadpan] Stoker'ın kaynakçasında adınız var: 'T., sigortacı.'
D17E_N_WHAT_LEGEND.en: [dry] You invented Dracula. [deadpan] Stoker's bibliography lists you: 'T., insurance agent.'

D17E_N_WHAT_NONE.tr: [dry] Hiçbir şey. [pause] Yalnız Topkapı'daki çocukluk defterinde fesli, ıslak bir adam resmi var. [deadpan] Altında soru işareti.
D17E_N_WHAT_NONE.en: [dry] Nothing. [pause] Except that the childhood notebook at Topkapı now has a drawing of a wet man in a fez. [deadpan] With a question mark underneath.

D17E_N_WHAT_POLICY.tr: [dry] Balkanlardaki ilk sigorta şirketi. [deadpan] Logosu kazık. [sighs] Beş yüz yıldır hasar ödemiyorlar.
D17E_N_WHAT_POLICY.en: [dry] The first insurance company in the Balkans. [deadpan] Its logo is a stake. [sighs] They haven't paid a claim in five hundred years.

D17E_R_01.tr: [curious] Merhaba! Sen de mi rehinesin? [quieter] Bizi önce Eğrigöz Kalesi'ne kapattılar: taş duvar, demir kapı. [relieved] Burası en azından aydınlık.
D17E_R_01.en: [curious] Hello! Are you a hostage too? [quieter] First they shut us up in Egrigöz fortress: stone walls, an iron door. [relieved] At least it's light here.

D17E_R_02.tr: [giggles] Abim her şeyi sivriltir. Kalemi bile. [laughing] Kaşığı bile!
D17E_R_02.en: [giggles] My brother sharpens everything. Even his pen. [laughing] Even his spoon!

D17E_R_03.tr: [shy] Abim burayı sevmiyor. [hesitant] Ben… alışıyorum. [brightening] Burada ders var, kitap var, ok var.
D17E_R_03.en: [shy] My brother doesn't like it here. [hesitant] I'm… getting used to it. [brightening] There are lessons here, books, archery.

D17E_R_KEB.tr: [eager] Mutfaktan kuzu getiririm. [grinning] Aşçıbaşı söylenir ama verir.
D17E_R_KEB.en: [eager] I'll get lamb from the kitchen. [grinning] The head cook grumbles, but he gives.

D17E_R_KEB_2.en: [gasps] [amazed] My brother smiled! He never smiles!

D17E_R_KEB_BACK.tr: [out of breath] [proudly] Aşçıbaşı kuzuyu verdi! Bir de soğan! [sniffles] Ağladım ama getirdim!
D17E_R_KEB_BACK.en: [out of breath] [proudly] The head cook gave me lamb! And onions! [sniffles] I cried, but I brought them!

D17E_R_LEG.en: [amazed] [whispers] My brother is writing for the first time!

D17E_R_LEG_0.en: [scared] [squeaky] Brother! There's a bat on the wall!

D17E_T_BACK_1.tr: [dazed] [slowly] Havuz vardı. Şehzade vardı. [nervous laugh] Bir de… Eflak.
D17E_T_BACK_1.en: [dazed] [slowly] There was a pool. There was a prince. [nervous laugh] And… Wallachia.

D17E_T_BOOK.tr: [proudly] Al. Tarih kitabı. [smug] Her şey yazıyor.
D17E_T_BOOK.en: [proudly] Here. A history book. [smug] It's all in there.

D17E_T_BRUTUS.tr: [storytelling] [dramatic] Sezar'ı en yakın adamı arkadan bıçakladı. Son sözü: [theatrical] 'Sen de mi Brütüs?'
D17E_T_BRUTUS.en: [storytelling] [dramatic] Caesar was stabbed in the back by his closest man. His last words: [theatrical] 'Et tu, Brute?'

D17E_T_BRUTUS_2.en: [whispers] [horrified] I shouldn't have said that. [panicked] I absolutely should not have said that.

D17E_T_CAL_1.tr: [relieved] Boş tarla. Güzel. [joking] Söz, tarlaya sigorta satmam.
D17E_T_CAL_1.en: [relieved] An empty field. Lovely. [joking] I promise not to sell insurance to a field.

D17E_T_CUBE.tr: [proudly] Rubik küpü. Kimse çözemez. [sheepish] Ben de çözemem.
D17E_T_CUBE.en: [proudly] A Rubik's cube. Nobody can solve it. [sheepish] I certainly can't.

D17E_T_CUBE_2.tr: [nervous] [whispers] Bunu Boğaz'a da uygulayacak, değil mi?
D17E_T_CUBE_2.en: [nervous] [whispers] He's going to do that to the Bosphorus, isn't he?

D17E_T_FEZ.tr: [alarmed] Fesim! Gel buraya… [relieved] Tamam. [sighs] Islak ama benim.
D17E_T_FEZ.en: [alarmed] My fez! Come here… [relieved] Got it. [sighs] Wet, but mine.

D17E_T_FLAT.en: [confidently] Flat. I read it on the internet.

D17E_T_GREEK.tr: [nervous] [fake confidence] Rum tüccarıyım. Zeytin, sünger… [salesman voice] sigorta.
D17E_T_GREEK.en: [nervous] [fake confidence] I'm a Greek merchant. Olives, sponges… [salesman voice] insurance.

D17E_T_HIT.tr: [pained] Ah! [indignant] 1444'te dayak yedim. [whining] Bunun sigortası yok!
D17E_T_HIT.en: [pained] Ow! [indignant] Caned in 1444. [whining] There's no policy for this!

D17E_T_HIZIR.tr: [hesitant] [going along with it] Evet. Hızır. [nervous laugh] Aceleyle geldim, ondan ıslağım.
D17E_T_HIZIR.en: [hesitant] [going along with it] Yes. Hızır. [nervous laugh] I came in a hurry, hence the wet.

D17E_T_KEB.tr: [friendly] [persuasive] Vlad. O sopalarla başka bir şey yapalım. [tempting] Bir parça et, biraz soğan, ateş…
D17E_T_KEB.en: [friendly] [persuasive] Vlad. Let's do something else with those sticks. [tempting] A bit of meat, an onion, a fire…

D17E_T_KEB_2.tr: [uneasy] Orman… şiş… olmaz. [hesitant] Yani olur. [forced cheer] Kebapsa olur.
D17E_T_KEB_2.en: [uneasy] A forest… of skewers… no. [hesitant] Well, yes. [forced cheer] If it's kebab, fine.

D17E_T_LEB.tr: [nervous] Heyecanlanınca leblebi yerim. Bir tane alayım… [gasps] Ay! [panicked] Kaçtı.
D17E_T_LEB.en: [nervous] I eat leblebi when I'm nervous. Just the one… [gasps] Oops! [panicked] It got away.

D17E_T_LEG.tr: [spooky storytelling] [slowly] Bir şato düşün. Gece. Yarasalar. [whispers] Pelerinli bir kont, kan içiyor. [dramatic] Sarımsaktan korkuyor…
D17E_T_LEG.en: [spooky storytelling] [slowly] Picture a castle. Night. Bats. [whispers] A count in a cape, drinking blood. [dramatic] Afraid of garlic…

D17E_T_LEG_2.tr: [uneasy] [nervous laugh] Çok. Beş yüz yıldır korkuyorlar.
D17E_T_LEG_2.en: [uneasy] [nervous laugh] Terribly. For five hundred years.

D17E_T_NONE.tr: [defensive] [talking fast] Karışmıyorum. Ben tanığım. Sözleşme var. [nervous] İmzaladım.
D17E_T_NONE.en: [defensive] [talking fast] I'm not getting involved. I'm a witness. There's a contract. [nervous] I signed it.

D17E_T_PANIC.tr: [panicked] [muttering to himself] Sivri sopalar. Ejderhanın oğlu. Eflak. [rising panic] Tolga, bir şey yap. Tarih seni izliyor.
D17E_T_PANIC.en: [panicked] [muttering to himself] Sharpened sticks. Son of the dragon. Wallachia. [rising panic] Tolga, do something. History is watching.

D17E_T_PHONE.tr: [startled] Annem arıyor. [confused] Burada nasıl çekiyor bu?
D17E_T_PHONE.en: [startled] It's my mum. [confused] How is there even signal here?

D17E_T_POL.tr: [salesman voice] [enthusiastic] Vlad. Bir gün kalen olacak, değil mi? [concerned] Kalen yanarsa, yıkılırsa? [pitching] Kale Kasko: yangın, deprem, Osmanlı…
D17E_T_POL.en: [salesman voice] [enthusiastic] Vlad. You'll have a castle one day, right? [concerned] What if it burns, collapses? [pitching] Castle Comprehensive: fire, earthquake, Ottomans…

D17E_T_ROUND.en: [confidently] Round. [proudly] There are even photos from space.

D17E_T_SALAD.tr: [blurting out] [cheerful] Sezar salata! Marul, kruton, parmesan…
D17E_T_SALAD.en: [blurting out] [cheerful] Caesar salad! Lettuce, croutons, parmesan…

D17E_T_SPLASH.tr: [spluttering] [shouting] Tarla bu mu?! [outraged] Boş tarla dediler, havuza düştüm!
D17E_T_SPLASH.en: [spluttering] [shouting] This is the field?! [outraged] They said an empty field and I've landed in a pool!

D17E_T_SPY.en: [panicked] [shouting] I'm not a spy, I'm in insurance!

D17E_T_STARS.tr: [awed] Bin yıldız… [self-deprecating] Ben AVM otoparkında arabamı bulamıyorum.
D17E_T_STARS.en: [awed] A thousand stars… [self-deprecating] I can't find my car in a shopping-centre car park.

D17E_T_TELL.tr: [serious] [quietly] Bu şehri sen alacaksın. [pause] Yirmi bir yaşında.
D17E_T_TELL.en: [serious] [quietly] You'll take this city. [pause] At twenty-one.

D17E_T_TIME.tr: [serious] [dramatic] Zaman yolcusuyum. Beş yüz seksen iki yıl sonrasından.
D17E_T_TIME.en: [serious] [dramatic] I'm a time traveller. From five hundred and eighty-two years ahead.

D17E_T_VENI.tr: [storytelling] [proudly] Julius Sezar. 'Veni, vidi, vici' demiş: geldim, gördüm, yendim.
D17E_T_VENI.en: [storytelling] [proudly] Julius Caesar. He said 'veni, vidi, vici': I came, I saw, I conquered.

D17E_T_WHAT_KEBAB.tr: [proudly] [excited] Kebap öğrettim. Kazık yerine şiş. [beaming] İyilik yaptım!
D17E_T_WHAT_KEBAB.en: [proudly] [excited] I taught him kebab. Skewers instead of stakes. [beaming] I did a good deed!

D17E_T_WHAT_LEGEND.tr: [sheepish] Bir hikâye anlattım. Vampirli. [nervous] Not aldı.
D17E_T_WHAT_LEGEND.en: [sheepish] I told a story. With a vampire. [nervous] He took notes.

D17E_T_WHAT_NONE.tr: [defensive] [shouting] Hiçbir şey! Karışmadım! [sheepish] Sadece biraz ıslandım.
D17E_T_WHAT_NONE.en: [defensive] [shouting] Nothing! I didn't interfere! [sheepish] I just got a bit wet.

D17E_T_WHAT_POLICY.tr: [proudly] Poliçe sattım. Vlad'a. [nervous] O da… [wincing] kazığı sevdi.
D17E_T_WHAT_POLICY.en: [proudly] I sold a policy. To Vlad. [nervous] He… [wincing] liked the stake.

D17E_V_01.tr: [cold] [proud] Babam ejderha. Ben ejderhanın oğluyum: Drăculea. [contemptuous] Sen kimsin, ıslak?
D17E_V_01.en: [cold] [proud] My father is the dragon. I am the dragon's son: Drăculea. [contemptuous] And who are you, wet one?

D17E_V_02.tr: [bitter] [flat] Babam bizi burada bıraktı. Şimdi duyduk ki Haçlılarla birlik oluyormuş. [darkly] Sultan bizi keser mi, merak ediyorum.
D17E_V_02.en: [bitter] [flat] Father left us here. Now we hear he's joining the crusaders. [darkly] I wonder whether the sultan will kill us.

D17E_V_04.tr: [sullen] Sen her şeye alışırsın, Radu. [quietly] [firm] Ben alışmam. Benim yerim Eflak.
D17E_V_04.en: [sullen] You get used to anything, Radu. [quietly] [firm] I don't. My place is Wallachia.

D17E_V_BURN.en: [flat] [annoyed] Turn them. Or we eat charcoal.

D17E_V_KEB_0.en: [flat] Here. Sharp. [suspicious] If that's what you want.

D17E_V_KEB_2.tr: [dreamy] [darkly] Bir gün bütün bir orman dolusu şiş yapacağım.
D17E_V_KEB_2.en: [dreamy] [darkly] One day I'll make a whole forest of skewers.

D17E_V_LEG.tr: [disgusted] Kan mı? İğrenç. [pause] [intrigued] Ama… insanlar ondan korkar mı?
D17E_V_LEG.en: [disgusted] Blood? Disgusting. [pause] [intrigued] But… are people afraid of him?

D17E_V_NONE.en: [cold] [staring] Were you going to say something, wet one?

D17E_V_POL.tr: [skeptical] [slowly] Yani ben sana altın veriyorum, sen bana bir kâğıt veriyorsun. [suspicious] Bir şey olursa da… madde 9?
D17E_V_POL.en: [skeptical] [slowly] So I give you gold, you give me a paper. [suspicious] And if something happens… clause 9?

D17E_V_POL_3.tr: [deadpan] Kazık. [slow smile] Beğendim. [darkly amused] Ben de herkese kazık atacağım.
D17E_V_POL_3.en: [deadpan] A stake. Through the purse. [slow smile] I like it. [darkly amused] I'll stake everyone.

D20O_U_EDIRNE_OK.tr: [gruff] [proud] Edirne'de direğin dibine inen gülle bu namludan çıkmıştı. [fatherly] Tunç sağlam, yamak; sen de elini sağlam tut.
D20O_U_EDIRNE_OK.en: [gruff] [proud] The ball that landed at the foot of the post in Edirne came out of this barrel. [fatherly] The bronze is sound, lad; keep your hands sound too.

D20O_U_EDIRNE_SHORT.tr: [gruff] [worried] Edirne'de kısa düşen gülleyi hatırlıyor musun, yamak? Tunç orada yoruldu. [grave] Bak, namlunun karnında ince bir çizgi: bu top güne bir çatlakla başlıyor.
D20O_U_EDIRNE_SHORT.en: [gruff] [worried] Remember the short shot in Edirne, lad? The bronze tired there. [grave] Look, a thin line on the barrel's belly: this gun starts the day with a crack.

D26_F_EDIRNE_GREEK.tr: [warm recognition] [slight smile] Sirtaki. [triumphant] Dediğim gibi: Kostantiniyye'de.
D26_F_EDIRNE_GREEK.en: [warm recognition] [slight smile] Sirtaki. [triumphant] As I said: in Constantinople.

D26_F_EDIRNE_HIZIR.tr: [warm recognition] [slight smile] Hızır. [triumphant] Dediğim gibi: Kostantiniyye'de.
D26_F_EDIRNE_HIZIR.en: [warm recognition] [slight smile] Hızır. [triumphant] As I said: in Constantinople.

D26_F_EDIRNE_TIME.tr: [warm recognition] [slight smile] Asansörlü. [triumphant] Dediğim gibi: Kostantiniyye'de.
D26_F_EDIRNE_TIME.en: [warm recognition] [slight smile] Lift man. [triumphant] As I said: in Constantinople.

D28O_U_EDIRNE_OK.tr: [gruff] [approving] Edirne'de gülleyi direğin dibine sen indirdin. [warmly] Nişan yine senin; bu sefer biraz daha gevşek tutsan da olur.
D28O_U_EDIRNE_OK.en: [gruff] [approving] In Edirne you put the ball at the foot of the post. [warmly] The aim is yours again; you can hold it a little looser this time.

D28O_U_EDIRNE_SHORT.tr: [gruff] [firm] Edirne'de nişan sendeydi, gülle direğe varmadı. [commanding] Bugün nişanı ben alırım. Sen doldur, tokmakla, çekil.
D28O_U_EDIRNE_SHORT.en: [gruff] [firm] In Edirne the aim was yours, and the ball never reached the post. [commanding] Today I aim. You load, ram and stand back.

D33O_F_EDIRNE_GREEK.tr: [delighted] [laughs] Sirtaki! [teasing] Rumcan düzeldi mi? [proudly] Benimki düzeldi.
D33O_F_EDIRNE_GREEK.en: [delighted] [laughs] Sirtaki! [teasing] Has your Greek improved? [proudly] Mine has.

D33O_F_EDIRNE_HIZIR.tr: [stunned] Sen… Edirne'deki havuz! [delighted] Hızır! [amazed] Sekiz yıl geçti, bir gün bile yaşlanmamışsın. [awed] Âb-ı hayatı buldun demek.
D33O_F_EDIRNE_HIZIR.en: [stunned] You… the pool at Edirne! [delighted] Hızır! [amazed] Eight years, and you haven't aged a day. [awed] So you did find the water of life.

D33O_F_EDIRNE_TIME.tr: [delighted] [laughs] Asansörlü! Sekiz yıl oldu. [amused] Arapçasını hâlâ bulamadım; Farsçası da yok.
D33O_F_EDIRNE_TIME.en: [delighted] [laughs] The lift man! Eight years. [amused] I still haven't found the Arabic for it; there's no Persian either.

REACT_CAMELEER_BOOK.tr: [curious] [hopeful] Deve resmi var mı? [disappointed] Yok mu? Kırk okkalık deve, kimsenin kitabına girmiyor. [sulking] Haksızlık.

REACT_CAMELEER_CHICKPEAS.tr: [excited] Leblebi! [talking fast] [worried] Deveye vermeyeyim, deve leblebiyi sever, sonra kırk bir okka olur, Ağa'nın cevabı değişir.

REACT_CAMELEER_COLOGNE.tr: [sniffs] [amazed] Deve kokusu gitti! Üç gündür gitmiyordu! [awed] Bu ne büyü!

REACT_CAMELEER_CUBE.tr: [counting] Altı yüzü var. [thoughtful] Devenin kaç yüzü var? Bir. [proudly] Ama iki hörgücü var. [nervous] İnşallah Ağa bunu sormaz.

REACT_CAMELEER_LIGHTER.tr: [surprised] Çakmaktaşı bu kadar küçük olur mu? [boasting] Benimki deve kadar... [flustered] yani deve kadar değil. [nervous laugh] Heyecandan.

REACT_CAMELEER_PHONE.tr: [gasps] [excited] Işıklı taş! Deveye göstersem deve şaşırır mı? [thoughtful] Şaşırmaz. Deve hiçbir şeye şaşırmaz. [laughs] Ben şaşırırım.

REACT_CAMELEER_POWERBANK.tr: [curious] Ağır mı bu? Kaç okka? [weighing it in his hand] Deveye yük olmaz. [groans] Bana olur.

REACT_CAMELEER_SELFIE.tr: [delighted] Resmimi mi yaptın? [excited] Deveyi de yap! Deve resimde iyi çıkar. [shy] Ben çıkmam, heyecandan.

REACT_CAMELEER_TAPE.tr: [curious] Bununla devenin yularını bağlasam kopmaz mı? [excited] Kopmaz mı? [breathless] Heyecanlandım.

REACT_CAMELEER_THERMOS.tr: [delighted] Sıcak çay! [dreamy] Çölde bu olsa... [sheepish] Ben çöle hiç gitmedim. Deve gitti. Ben dinledim.

D3_R_11.tr: [bored] 1453 mü? [rummaging] Bakayım... Fötr şapka, yelek, daktilo. [matter-of-fact] Paket bu.

D3_R_14B.tr: [dry] O fes yanlış rafta. 1829 rafında olacaktı. [sighs] Depoda da anomali var ama onu kimse denetlemiyor.

D3_R_15.tr: [sly] Şapka size yakıştı. 1453'te kimse fark etmez. [chuckles] Ya da herkes sizi başka biri sanar. [shrugging] Her ikisi de olur.

D3_R_IDLE.tr: [bored] [slowly] İade yok. Değişim yok. [dry] Zaman da yok.

D3_R_KIT_1.tr: [lazily] Bir de yeni yönetmelik paketi var: Kaldırma Formu Z-9 ve Zaman Perdesi. [matter-of-fact] F ile uçulur, Q ile görünmez olunur.

D3_R_KIT_3.tr: [warning] Görünürken uçmayın. İnsanlar görür, efsane olur. [weary] Efsane de iş çıkarır. [knowing] Ben bilirim, depoda üç tane var.

D8_A2_ENTER.tr: [formal] Görevdeyiz. [wistful] ...Ama sonra olabilir. Sonra. Görevden sonra. [softly] Şekersiz.

D8_A2_RECALL.tr: [politely] [wistful] Çayı sonra içeriz, Cemil Bey. [sighs] Sonra. Toplantıdan sonra.

D8_A2_UNKNOWN.tr: [mild] Bu saatte hırdavatçıda bir amca. Normal. [focused] Biz garajdaki adamı arıyoruz; o bütün gece bir kez bile ışığa çıkmadı.
D8_A2_UNKNOWN.en: [mild] An old man at the hardware store at this hour. Normal. [focused] We're after the garage guy; he never stepped into the light once all night.

D8_A_CAUGHT_2.tr: [weary] Yine siz. [polite suspicion] Bu sepette ne var? ...Bir kondansatör? Ne için? [formal] Not ediyorum. Kasaya.

D10G_C_1.tr: [impressed] Çandarlı'nın mührü! [lowered voice] [looks around] Bu mektubu ancak ben Venedik'e götürürüm. [firm] Ama taşıyan da gelir. Kural bu.

D10G_C_3.tr: [impatient] Pazartesi ne? Çan ikinci kez çalınca kalkıyoruz. [blunt] Ya bin ya mektubu geri götür.

D10G_C_EARLY.tr: [gruff] İskele dolu. Yükümüz var, yolcumuz yok. [dismissive] Git.

D10G_C_MISSED.tr: [shouting from the deck] [mocking] Venedik beklemez, Frenk! Mektubunu Sultan'ına ver!

D10G_C_TO_FATIH.tr: [incredulous] Sadrazamın mektubunu Sultan'a mı? [laughs] Sen ya çok dürüstsün ya çok aptal. [amused] İkisi de Venedik'te iş bulamaz.

D10G_C_VENICE.tr: [hearty] Venedik'e hoş geldin, Frenk. Üç ay sürer. [chuckles] İyi denizciysen iki buçuk.

D10O_CAMELEER_1.tr: [anxious] [talking fast] Üçüncü kez sıradayım. Üçüncü soruda hep yanıyorum. Deveyle ilgili soruyor, bilmiyorum. [exasperated] Devem biliyor ama o konuşmuyor.

D10O_CAMELEER_2.tr: [excited] Kırk okka. Kırk! Her gün sayıyorum. [sheepish] Ağa'ya söylemeyi hiç akıl edemedim. [nervous laugh] Heyecandan.

D13_R_CARD_OK.tr: [long pause] [squinting] ...Fotoğrafta pijama var. [grudgingly impressed] Ama laminasyon kusursuz. Geçin. [solemn] Laminasyona saygım var.

D13_R_OPEN.tr: [lazily] Kapı açık. Nihat Bey açık bırakmış. 'Yaşlı bir beyefendi gelecek' dedi. [skeptical] Siz misiniz? [dry] Pijamayla?

D27_C_1.tr: [gruff] Venedik gemisi, Venedik yolcusu. Yer kalmadı, sormayın. [pointed] Bu sefer kaçak yolcu da yok.

D17O_K_COME.en: [shouting] [excited] Frank! We've emptied the pots and brought the buckets! [commanding] Boys, get in line!

D17O_K_DAWN.en: [tired] [proud] My pots are empty and my buckets are wet. [chuckles] The Sultan's galley is saved; he owes me a ladle.

D17O_K_DAWN_BURNED.en: [sighs] The stern burned, but the hull still floats. [wry] Same in the kitchen: the bottom of the pot catches, the meal survives.

D17_G_HELP.en: [shouting] [urgent] New man! Two of us from Cattaneo's ship. [grateful] On 20 April you cut the ropes at the rail; the captain said "go pay your debt". [determined] We'll hold the rope, you pull!

D17_K_BRIDGE.en: [gruff] Whatever you are. Mahmud the bridge-builder needs hands; you'll haul barrels and eat his bread. [menacing] Try running and the water's still right there.

D17_K_NET.en: [surprised] [shouting] Look at the net! Not a fish, a man. [suspicious] Doesn't look Greek, doesn't look Frankish. Who are you, man?

D17_L_CHAIN.en: [excited] [shouting] Chickpea Frank! Three nights without sleep, and we couldn't if we tried! [urgent] We've got the lantern on them: three heads in the water!

D17_N_CAM_1.en: [formal] [proudly] The Bureau's recording camera. Model Z-0, instant print. [matter-of-fact] You take the picture, the file prints it.

D17_N_CAM_2.en: [dry] A phone picture gets deleted, Mr Tolga. [firm] This one drops into your hand, gets signed and goes in the file. Here.

D17_N_CAM_3.en: [instructive] A test frame. Point it at me; once I'm in the viewfinder, press the shutter.

D17_N_CAM_4.en: [deadpan] I've closed my eyes. Everyone closes their eyes in a Bureau photograph. [dry] That's how it goes in the file.

D17_N_CAPTIVE.en: [over a crackling radio] [concerned] Mr Tolga, your signal is coming from the far shore of the Horn. The Bureau can't collect you now: [grave] you'll write one page from the other side. [reassuring] We'll fetch you afterwards.

D17_N_FIRST_36.en: [formal] One correction, Mr Tolga: the file was opened three weeks earlier. The first entry is 9 April, before dawn. Giustiniani's men are going out beyond the walls, and so are you. [dry] You can run, can't you?

D17_N_LIFT.en: [calm] Into the lift, Mr Tolga. I'll set the dial; you face the door and breathe.

D17_TR_LOST.en: [panicked] [shouting] Overboard again! The rope won't reach... [desperate] The guns! Back! Pull back!

D17_TR_SHORT.en: [urgent] Cattaneo's men have been patching up the carrack since 20 April; they couldn't spare us oarsmen tonight. [tense] We're short-handed, Bureau man. Be quick!

D17_TR_WARN.en: [angry] [shouting] Fall in again and the rope won't reach you, insurance man! Keep away from the rail!

D17_T_CAM_1.en: [skeptical] Mr Nihat, this camera is older than my grandfather. [pleading] Can't I just use my phone?

D17_T_CAPTIVE.en: [nervous laugh] Was there a 'taken prisoner' clause in the policy? There wasn't. [sighs] I know, because I wrote it.

D17_T_CHAIN.en: [whispers] [disbelief] They ate two. They're still talking.

D17_T_NET.en: [spluttering] [flustered] I'm in insurance. I mean... a loss assessor. [sheepish] A wet loss assessor.

D18_HA_01.en: [cheerful] Fez boy! Building a bridge? [friendly] We'll hold the barrels, you tie. Beats guard duty.

D18_HU_01.en: [confident] I'm Hasan. [confused] ...I'm not. [correcting himself] I'm Hüseyin. And I'm the one holding the barrel.

D18_HU_01_HUFEZ.en: [proudly] The one in the fez is Hüseyin. That's me. [cheerful] I'll hold the barrel; you tie the rope.

D18_N_01_CAPTIVE.en: [over a crackling radio] [dry] Mr Tolga, this page is on the Ottoman side, and this time you weren't invited. The boatmen handed you to the bridge-builder. The Bureau will fetch you at the end of the page; [pause] until then... work.

D18_N_END_CAPTIVE.en: [formal] Recorded. We're taking you back, Mr Tolga: the Byzantine record resumes on the night of 3 May. [deadpan] Don't return the wet clothes to the Bureau.

D18_T_01_CAPTIVE.en: [nervous] Master, I'm actually from the other side. I mean... from no side. [weak laugh] I'm in insurance.

D18_T_END_CAPTIVE.en: [tired] [thoughtful] I built a bridge. For the other side. [softly] But the knots are mine; whoever crosses it, let them cross safely.

D18_U_01_CAPTIVE.en: [gruff] You're the one they fished out? You're wet, but your hands work. [matter-of-fact] Here prisoners work and Janissaries work; the bread's the same for all.

D18_U_02_CAPTIVE.en: [puzzled] Insurance? What's that, some kind of prayer? [brisk] Here's the order: barrel pair into the water, lash with rope, lay the planks. Six sections.

D18_U_TAPE.en: [curious] What's that? Sticky rope? [impressed] ...You wrapped it over the hawser and the knot stayed put. [amazed] They don't have this in Venice.

D18_U_TAPE_2.en: [amused] Again? [chuckles] Let's hope the Sultan doesn't count the strips when he crosses.

D18_U_TWINS.en: [amazed] Two Janissaries holding barrels. Never seen it in my life. [pleased] Hold on, then: if the barrel doesn't move, the knot doesn't slip.

D19O_R_HOOKS_BAD.en: [suspicious] ...Wait a moment. Weren't you the oarsman whose hooks wouldn't hold on Baltaoğlu's galley on 20 April? [cold] Powder's short; two shots are yours, don't waste them.

D19O_R_HOOKS_OK.en: [impressed] They tell it all over the fleet: on 20 April you were the oarsman whose hook held on Baltaoğlu's galley. [approving] A hand that holds a hook holds a gun; five shots are yours.

D19_C_01_CAPTIVE.en: [excited] You! They saw you hauling barrels on the Turks' bridge, and you got away. [scheming] You've got Turkish and you know barrels: just our man. If anyone asks, you do the talking.

D19_C_GRAIN_HALF.en: [conspiratorial] The crew counts your vote as half, Bureau man. [warmly] I've written it down as a whole one anyway.

D19_C_REPORT_TEZKIRE.en: [hesitant] And... we got past the patrol on this Frank's paper, Niko. [lowered voice] The Sultan's tughra.

D19_C_TEZKIRE.en: [through gritted teeth] The Sultan's paper, on a Venetian ship. [suspicious] Whose man are you, Bureau man?

D19_C_TEZKIRE_2.en: [dry] Supplementary cover. The crew saw it. [warning] They won't forget it at the vote.

D19_NK_TEZKIRE.en: [surprised] Tolga's? [softly] ...Let him keep it. [grave] If the city falls, that paper will save a life.

D19_N_END_TEZKIRE.en: [formal] Recorded: 3 May to 23 May. The sources say the crew voted to return. No source says an Ottoman patrol bowed to a Venetian ship. [dry] Your footnote is getting longer, Mr Tolga.

D19_P_TEZKIRE.en: [startled] The Sultan's tughra... [humbly] Forgive us, sir, we didn't know. [respectful] Clear sailing to you!

D19_S2_SAVED.en: [firm] And there's this: on the night of 28 April this man pulled me out of the Horn. [heartfelt] I owe that city a life.

D19_S2_TEZKIRE_RETURN.en: [quietly] Leave him be. The man with the paper is going back to die with us. [moved] That's enough for me.

D19_S_GRAIN_BAD.en: [bitter] One more thing. On 20 April I was on the grain ship, lashed to Cattaneo's carrack. This man was on that deck, and the ship came in wounded. [cold] His vote counts as half to me.

D19_S_GRAIN_FLEE.en: [vindicated] Even the man who cut the ropes says "save ourselves". You see? I'm not alone.

D19_S_GRAIN_OK.en: [earnest] One more thing. On 20 April I was on the grain ship, lashed to Cattaneo's carrack. This is the man who cut the grappling ropes. [loyal] I'll vote the way he votes.

D19_S_GRAIN_RETURN.en: [resolved] The man who cut the ropes says "we go back". Then I go back too. [sad smile] My wife can wait.

D19_S_TEZKIRE.en: [suspicious] Show us your paper first, Frank. If the Sultan's man says "go back", it's a trap; [darkly] if he says "run", it's worse.

D19_S_TEZKIRE_FLEE.en: [accusing] See? The Sultan's man doesn't want us back in the city.

D19_T_01_CAPTIVE.en: [defensive] I didn't escape. I signed a form and a door opened. [sighs] ...Yes, I speak Turkish. [self-deprecating] My experience with disguises still stops at the fez.

D19_T_TEZKIRE.en: [confident] Captain, bring your lantern over here. [knowing] You'll know the tughra.

D19_T_TEZKIRE_2.en: [salesman voice] I'm an insurer, captain. I've got a policy with everyone. [smug] This is... supplementary cover.

D20O_T_TAPE.en: [confident] One moment, master. [proudly] A hairline crack gets a hairline fix.

D20O_U_01_ULIGHTER.en: [delighted] [shouting] You! The one in the fez! The apprentice who left me his fire box! [proudly] Look, it still strikes. [brisk] Today I need hands.

D20O_U_BED_CROOKED.en: [worried] Ever since the sled slipped that day, the bed has sat crooked. [firm] Keep your aim tight; a ball that strays even a little won't count.

D20O_U_BED_SOUND.en: [approving] The bed settled first time that day; you carried the rollers. [warmly] This gun knows your hands; even if it strays a little, it marks the wall.

D20O_U_FLAW.en: [grave] But listen: I told you those moulds were Serbian work. There's a bubble in the bronze's belly. [ominous] This gun starts the day with a crack.

D20O_U_LESS.en: [urgent] A cracked barrel doesn't get a full charge. [shouting] Half measure! The ball will fall short: raise the muzzle!

D20O_U_NAME_1.en: [fond] Look: Monday. You named it; I haven't forgotten. [chuckles] Today's the longest day of the week for the Greeks.

D20O_U_NAME_2.en: [fond] Look: Parcel. You named it; I haven't forgotten. [hopeful] Hold like the cloth, you said; today we'll see if it holds.

D20O_U_NAME_3.en: [fond] Look: Insurance. You named it; I haven't forgotten. [laughs] Covers everything, you said; today it covers all the damage to the wall.

D20O_U_NAME_4.en: [whispers] [conspiratorial] Look: Cube. I told no one; the army calls it 'the Great Gun'. You call it that too.

D20O_U_NAME_GONE.en: [sad] The gun you named blew up in April, lad; I haven't forgotten. [proud] This is its big brother. [quietly] Nobody names this one.

D20O_U_TAPED.en: [tense] Tick... Wait. [amazed] It held! [laughs] That sticky strip of yours! Still there. [proudly] The bronze complained, but the strip didn't let go.

D20O_U_TAPE_AGAIN.en: [amused] More strip? [laughs] Half this gun will be bronze and half your strip.

D20O_U_TAPE_NEW.en: [skeptical] A sticky strip? ...Will it hold bronze? [listening carefully] [impressed] It holds. I haven't named it, but it holds.

D20_G_01_KNOWN_GBOOK.en: [warm] The insurance man! [troubled] I read your book. One page keeps me up at night. We'll talk later. [brisk] You came empty-handed; here, empty hands carry.

D20_G_01_KNOWN_GLIGHTER.en: [warm] The insurance man! [proudly] Your lighter's with me; my gunners light fuses even in the rain. You came empty-handed. Good. [brisk] Here, empty hands carry.

D20_G_01_KNOWN_WARNED.en: [warm] The insurance man! [wry] Look, the shield's always on my right: I'm minding my right shoulder. You came empty-handed. Good. [brisk] Here, empty hands carry.

D20_G_GUN_GLIGHTER.en: [urgent] Frank! Take this, it came from Genoa. [grinning] I lit its match with your lighter, first time. [warning] It kicks, keep it on your shoulder!

D20_G_LEON_LOST.en: [somber] Still no word of Leon, not since April. [quietly] Tonight the breach is one archer short.

D20_G_LEON_OK.en: [warmly] Leon is at the breach tonight, beside you. [moved] He says he's come to pay his debt.

D20_NK_01.en: [cheerful] [out of breath] Tolga! I'm off watch tonight; I'll haul the planks, you see to the barrels!

D20_NK_DROP.en: [straining] One load from me! [encouraging] Don't stop counting, Frank.

D21O_D_LISTEN_K.en: [impressed] Your ear hasn't forgotten the earth, fez. [chuckles] You'd have made a miner.

D21O_T_LISTEN_FIRST.en: [whispers] Wait. [listening] Tap... tap... [tense] Someone's digging from the other side, towards us. I heard it just like this in April.

D21_G_01_CAPTIVE.en: [cool] The scribe who fell off the wall at Blachernae. I'm Johannes Grant. [businesslike] The guards gave you to me: you speak Turkish, so tonight you're my ears, and later my tongue.

D21_G_CAP1_CAPTIVE.en: [suspicious] You're a Turk, and so is he. Ask him: where are the other tunnels? [threatening] Translate it wrong and I'll know, scribe.

D21_K_CAPTIVE.en: [bitter] I saw you at Blachernae, scribe. You're the one they threw off the ladder. [contemptuous] Now you speak their tongue?

D21_N_01_CAPTIVE.en: [over a crackling radio] [dry] Mr Tolga, this page is the Greeks' record and you are a prisoner. The Bureau will fetch you at the end of the page. [firm] Until then, do Grant's work.

D21_N_END_CAPTIVE.en: [formal] We're taking you back, Mr Tolga: the Ottoman record resumes on the night of 17 May. [deadpan] Grant will be told you escaped.

D21_T_01_CAPTIVE.en: [nervous] I'm not a scribe. Well, this week I am. [earnest] Really I'm in insurance: I don't take sides, I assess.

D21_T_CAPTIVE_K.en: [softly] [sincere] I speak both tongues. Tonight they're both asking the same thing: that nobody dies.

D21_T_EAR.en: [whispers] Hang on. In April, under the ground, I learned to listen. [thoughtful] An ear is a bowl too.

D21_T_THERMOS.en: [apologetic] Sorry, tea. [determined] I've filled the lid with water; that's the last bowl.

D22O_HU_01.en: [eager] Wherever Hasan goes, I go. I'm Hüseyin. [proudly] ...This time I'm sure.

D22O_HU_01_HUFEZ.en: [cheerful] The one in the fez is Hüseyin, that's me. Wherever Hasan goes, I go. [eager] I'll carry baskets and nail hides too.

D22O_HU_CARRY.en: [coughing] [shouting] The last one's mine! [out of breath] [proud] My eyebrows are gone, but the carpenter's here.

D22O_H_BLAKH_BAD.en: [gruff] You've been limping since they threw you off the wall at Blachernae, clerk. [warning] You'll carry the basket slowly; when the arrows come, don't be far from cover.

D22O_H_BLAKH_OK.en: [impressed] You're the clerk who beat the Greek on the wall at Blachernae, aren't you? The company's talking about you. [protective] Tonight I'll shout "Cover!" early when the arrows come; you run early too.

D22O_H_CAPTIVE.en: [surprised] Hold on... Are you the clerk who was left at the foot of the wall at Blachernae, the one the Greeks took? They say you were interpreting in Grant's mine! How did you get back? ...Tell me later; the aghas will ask too. You're limping; you'll carry the basket slowly.

D22_G_BLAKH_BAD.en: [frustrated] They got onto the wall at Blachernae, clerk; all the good fuse went that night. [warning] These were cut in a hurry: some burn short, some long. Don't take your eyes off them.

D22_G_BLAKH_OK.en: [proud] Clerk, the Emperor asked about the man who held the wall-walk at Blachernae; I told him it was you. [confident] Tonight his own gunner cut your fuses: they burn evenly, you won't miss the moment.

D22_G_COLOGNE.en: [sniffs] [puzzled] What's that smell? ...Not wine. [grim satisfaction] Worse than wine. Good.

D22_G_SOAKED.en: [shouting] [exultant] You let go early, but they couldn't kick it! The cologne barrel rolled down burning and the base caught!

D22_T_COLOGNE.en: [mischievous] One moment. [proudly] Lemon cologne, eighty proof. Wet hides won't stand up to this.

D23_I_LETTER.en: [formal] [warm] You're the one who brought the Emperor's April letter to the Sultan. Today's offer is its answer; the Sultan will be pleased it passes through your tongue again.

D23_TH_PASS.en: [surprised] This... is my feast-day permit! A single seal. [pleased] Now it has two: palace interpreter. [warmly] Look after it until it has seven.

D23_T_PASS.en: [delighted] I've been promoted. [wry] Seven years in insurance couldn't get me a title; one sheet of paper just did.

D23_T_SINGED.en: [sheepish] They stayed at the tower. The tower burned, and so did they. [hastily] It won't get in the way of translating.

D24O_K_MENU_1.en: [proud] Know what's in the pot? Your feast soup: tarhana. [warmly] From the Sultan's table to the army's cauldron.

D24O_K_MENU_2.en: [proud] Know what's in the pot? Your feast soup: lentil. [warmly] From the Sultan's table to the army's cauldron.

D24O_K_MENU_BURNED.en: [teasing] I tried the soup you burned at the feast again, in this pot. [chuckles] It didn't burn this time. Neither did the kitchen.

D24O_K_THERMOS.en: [pleased] I filled that magic flask of yours with soup too; it's been piping hot for three hours. [brisk] I'll take it to the fire nearest the kitchen; you see to the others.

D24O_S_1_THERMOS.en: [amazed] The head cook's red flask! The moon's going dark, but the soup's still boiling. [relieved] So not everything goes dark.

D24O_S_TEA.en: [awed] [softly] Hot... [superstitious] That must be why the moon's gone red. It's boiling.

D24O_T_ECLIPSE_AGAIN.en: [uneasy] I saw this in April too. From a cell in the walls, a month early. [whispers] Is it going dark twice because of me?

D24O_T_TEA.en: [calm] [warmly] Tea. The moon will wait; it's not going anywhere. Tea goes cold.

D24_NK_01.en: [earnest] Tolga! I've handed my watch over for an hour. [loyal] I'll walk beside you; if the wind comes, I'll put my shoulder to the pole.

D24_NK_KID.en: [urgent] [shouting] I'm laying a door across the porch! It'll hold the water back. You fetch the boy!

D24_NK_LATE.en: [shocked] He ran! ...Uphill, to the dry side. [hopeful] [trembling] He'll make it, Tolga. He'll make it.

D24_NK_SAVED.en: [out of breath] [relieved] The boy's dry. You're soaked, and so am I. [laughing] But the boy's dry.

D24_T_ECLIPSE.en: [to himself] [uneasy] They say the moon went dark two nights ago. I saw it a month early, in April, from a cell window. [whispers] Did this city's moon go dark twice, or did I come too early?

D24_T_NK_01.en: [warm] Niko. Glad you came. [sad] No jokes today, I promised; [soft laugh] so don't make me laugh.

D25_G_TEZKIRE.en: [shouting] Stop, kitchen boy! [suspicious] ...What's this? [reverent] My Sultan's tughra. Very well. [warning] But I've got my eye on you.

D25_K_CANDLE.en: [excited] [breathless] Stranger! The stranger from the eaves! I found my mother, she was at the market. [happy] She lit a candle for you too.

D25_K_PASS.en: [solemn] [warm] The palace interpreter. You carried my words to the Sultan's envoy exactly as I spoke them. [humbly] Forgive me too, Frank.

D25_K_PASS_SOFT.en: [solemn] [knowing] The palace interpreter. You softened my words a little; I know. [gently] I have forgiven it. [humbly] Forgive me too, Frank.

D25_T_MARCO.en: [softly] [tender] Don't leave your mother's side tonight, little one. [urgent whisper] Not for a moment.

D26O_AB_LADDER_BAD.en: [weary] [bitter] Clerk... On 18 April that stockade didn't give us a scratch. This is what's left of my company. [warning] Keep your head down; stones are coming.

D26O_AB_LADDER_OK.en: [excited] [shouting] Clerk! You were the one who tore the stockade down with a hook on 18 April. We'll hold the top of the ladder; shields up!

D26O_K_WATER.en: [shouting] [brisk] Frank! The buckets are on me, you're the water-boy. My kitchen boy is watering the first company; you run to the other two!

D26_G_25_BAD.en: [grim] If you didn't hear it, we don't know. [determined] We'll meet every wave like the first.

D26_G_25_OK.en: [thoughtful] [calculating] The expendable men first... Then the first of the oil goes to the foot of the ladders; few will make it up the first ladder. [grim] I'll save my best for the Janissaries.

D26_G_DUCK.en: [gasps] [shaken] ...Frank. A finger lower and... [weak laugh] I owe you a wine.

D26_G_DUCK_GBOOK.en: [gasps] [shaken] ...That line wasn't in your book, Frank. [wondering] You again.

D26_G_HURT_GBOOK.en: [pained] [gasping] It went through the breastplate... Your book was right. [weak] Take me... take me to the ship.

D26_G_HURT_WARNED.en: [pained] My right shoulder... [bitter] You told me in April, Frank. I didn't listen. [weak] Take me to the ship; I'll have it bound and come back.

D26_G_LIGHTER_BACK.en: [weak] [gentle] Take it. My gunners never paid their week. Neither did I. [sad smile] ...Keep it.

D26_G_NOTRUST_GBOOK.en: [proud] [defiant] Get down? I read your book, Frank. The twenty-ninth of May, this very spot. [scoffing] Who changes what's written—

D26_G_NOTRUST_WARNED.en: [irritated] Get down? In April it was my shoulder, now this... [proud] I am Giustiniani, Frank. I do not—

D26_I_KASIM_FREE.en: [whispers] [trembling] I'm walking out on a miner's word, Frank. I'm nobody now. [relieved] I'm leaving as nobody.

D26_I_TEZ_FREE.en: [whispers] [wry] It's an honour to be your clerk, Frank. I'm nobody now. [relieved] I'm leaving as nobody.

D26_KS_1.en: [warm] [excited] Interpreter! Remember me? Kasım. Grant kept his word: the tunnels burned empty, nobody was left inside. [relieved] And this morning our lot opened my cell door.

D26_KS_1_FIRE.en: [warm] Interpreter! Remember me? Kasım. [sad] Mirko's face is still burned, but he's alive. [relieved] And Grant kept his word: the tunnels burned empty. This morning our lot opened my cell door.

D26_KS_FREE.en: [firm] [pleading] Agha! This old man is the interpreter's clerk. If I came out of that tunnel alive, it was on this man's word. Let him go.

D26_N_KASIM_FREE.en: [softly] The sources say he escaped; they don't say how. On a sapper's word... [warm] I won't put this in the file either, Mr Tolga.

D26_N_PHONE_BACK.en: [formal] One more thing, Mr Tolga: the Bureau's issued phone. The return form's right here. [puzzled] ...Fourteen percent. [deadpan] Always fourteen percent.

D26_N_TEZ_FREE.en: [softly] The sources say he escaped; they don't say how. ...Now we know. [warm] I won't put this in the file, Mr Tolga.

D26_S_KASIM_FREE.en: [indifferent] The sapper's interpreter, the interpreter's clerk... Take him. [dismissive] One old man less; nobody's counting.

D26_S_TEZ_FREE.en: [reverent] My Sultan's tughra... [dismissive] Take your clerk. One old man less; nobody's counting.

D26_T_25_BAD.en: [apologetic] Last night I got as far as the pavilion, but the guards chased me off twice. [sad] I didn't hear how it ended.

D26_T_25_OK.en: [urgent] [lowered voice] Last night I was at the back wall of the Turkish pavilion. I heard the Sultan: first the azaps, then the Anatolian troops, last the Janissaries.

D26_T_AYA_CANDLE.en: [softly] [moved] Last night I lit a candle here. The others have gone out. Mine is still burning. [awed] Soldiers everywhere, and it's burning.

D26_T_KASIM_ASK.en: [urgent] [quietly] Kasım, that white-bearded man in the column... he's my clerk. [firm] Now you keep a word.

D26_T_LIGHTER_BACK.en: [softly] [choked up] The lighter's still warm. Forty days in a Genoese pocket.

D26_T_LIGHTER_KEEP.en: [gentle] [sad smile] No room in the bag. You keep it; you'll light a match on the ship.

D26_T_PHONE_BACK.en: [wry] I didn't charge it once in a month. [amused] It was always fourteen percent.

D26_T_TEZ_FREE.en: [firm] [confident] Agha! This old man is my clerk. The Sultan's warrant: here's the tughra, here's my name.

D27_B_1.en: [warm] [tired] Bureau man! From the brigantine. Twenty days of empty sea, remember? [sad] The city fell. We'd gone back all the same.

D27_B_FLEE.en: [rueful] You said "save ourselves". You were right. [quietly] I've got a berth on Morosini's ship; nobody's voting this time.

D27_B_RETURN.en: [proud] You said "go back". I don't regret it. Morosini's offering me a berth, but I'm staying: [determined] every ship that leaves this shore will need a captain.

D27_B_TEZKIRE.en: [thoughtful] The night you showed that paper with the tughra, nobody in the crew slept. [sad] Now I get it: everyone should have had a paper.

D27_GN_AGAIN.en: [cool] Keep your ledger well, customs man.

D27_GN_FOUND.en: [surprised] [wry] The customs man from Rumeli Hisarı! The man who found the fifth item in my hold last August. [chuckles] The one under the hemp.

D27_GN_GO.en: [bitter] You drank my wine and deleted a line. If the charter's lines get deleted like that too... [resigned] I'm leaving, customs man. For Chios.

D27_GN_MISSED.en: [smug] The quick customs man from Rumeli Hisarı! Last August you wrote down four items. [dry] The fifth reached Galata; now that's the Sultan's too.

D27_GN_STAY.en: [respectful] And you wouldn't take my wine. If men like you are going to keep the Sultan's charter, I'm staying. [warm] My ledger stays too.

D27_I_THANKS.en: [warm] [grateful] The man with the tughra paper. I'm going to Rome. I owe you a prayer, Frank. [chuckles] And a hat.

D27_I_THANKS_KASIM.en: [moved] A miner's word, an interpreter's tongue... I'm going to Rome, Frank. I owe you a prayer. [softly] And one for Kasım.

D27_N_BRIG.en: [dry] Recognise the captain at the foot of the gangway, Mr Tolga? You spent twenty days on the same deck.

D27_N_GENOESE.en: [dry] Look at the Genoese by those chests, Mr Tolga. Last August at Boğazkesen you searched his ship.

D27_N_ISI.en: [softly] Look at the white beard in the queue for the ship, Mr Tolga. Look familiar?

D27_T_B_FLEE.en: [warm] Safe travels, captain. [softly] May the wind be behind you this time.

D27_T_B_RETURN.en: [earnest] Stay, captain. Someone has to meet the ships that come back.

D27_T_GN_GO.en: [sheepish] One line short, one bottle extra... [sighs] You're right. Safe travels.

D27_T_GN_STAY.en: [sincere] The declaration was complete. The charter will be read out complete too. [warm] Stay.

D27_T_I_THANKS.en: [playful] Forget the hat, Cardinal. [chuckles] The red was drawing too much attention anyway.

D28O_U_ROAD_BAD.en: [worried] The bridge gave way on the Edirne road and the sled's runner cracked. [firm] You'll set the rollers often, clerk, or it slips.

D28O_U_ROAD_OK.en: [approving] The drovers know you from the road; you got them over that bridge. [confident] The sled won't slip even if you set fewer rollers.

D30O_AZ_WRONG.en: [panicked] [shouting] Not this way! Very much not this way!

D30O_A_LATE.en: [out of breath] [triumphant] Made it! Where's the fight? [confused] …Back? [resigned] Right, I'm back too.

D30O_D_CHASE.en: [shouting] [triumphant] They're running! Push them off the wall!

D30O_G_CAPTIVE.en: [curious] Is this the scribe who fell off the wall? Broken leg, working tongue. Does he speak Turkish? ...He does. God's grace: I need an interpreter. Lift him up.

D30O_N_CAPTIVE.en: [over a crackling radio] [concerned] Mr Tolga, your signal is coming from inside the walls. You'll write one page in the Greek record: in Grant's mine. [reassuring] The Bureau will fetch you afterwards.

D30O_T_CAPTIVE.en: [deadpan] Promoted from scribe to prisoner. [sarcastic] Any change in pay?

D30O_T_DONTLOOK.en: [nervous] [muttering] Don't look down. Don't look down. [terrified] …Looked.

D30O_T_DOWN_OK.en: [out of breath] [relieved] I jumped off the last rung and the ladder went over behind me. [wry] First thing tonight that happened on time.

D30O_T_FLOOD.en: [alarmed] The wall-walk filled up all at once. They keep pouring out of the tower doors, spears pointed at us. [nervous laugh] And we were calling this a win.

D30O_T_PANIC.en: [panicked] Right, heroics are over. [shouting] Where's the ladder?!

D30O_T_RIDE.en: [dazed] I didn't bring the ladder down; the ladder brought me down. And there was a bush. [grateful] Bless that bush.

D30O_T_SHOVED.en: [groaning] Someone shouldered me off the wall. A bush caught me. [wry] Tonight I trust bushes more than people.

D30O_T_WOBBLE.en: [panicked] [shouting] No no no, leave it! Leave the ladder alone!

D30_D_GUNNER_BAD.en: [skeptical] Are you the gunner from the Horn? We heard your shot went into the water. [cold] Powder's short; three shots for you.

D30_D_GUNNER_OK.en: [impressed] Are you the gunner from the Horn? We heard you hit the bridge. [eager] Five shots for you: bring down the ladder-bearers.

D31O_TW_39_BAD.en: [cold] [resentful] You're the clerk from Petrion. The banner reached our street late; my neighbour's door was broken. If you want rope, knock on another door.

D31O_TW_39_OK.en: [grateful] Clerk! You're the one who put the banner on our door in time in Petrion. [urgent] Here, our well rope. Lower the child with it.

D31O_T_39_BAD.en: [sighs] Fair enough. [determined] I'll climb with both hands, then.

D31O_T_39_OK.en: [warm] A banner saved a door, the door brought a rope. [proud] In insurance that's called reinsurance.

D32O_AZ_25_BUNDLE.en: [shouting] [encouraging] The Head Cook's lad has already thrown the first bundle. The rest is yours, clerk!

D32O_K_25_BAD.en: [stern] Last night the guard sent you back to the kitchen twice from behind the pavilion, and he told me too. [lowered voice] I'll tell you how the council ended: fasting today, the assault tomorrow. [firm] No lad for you today; every bundle is yours.

D32O_K_25_OK.en: [conspiratorial] Last night the guards searched behind the pavilion for an apprentice and never found him. It was you, I know; keep your mouth shut and so will I. [warm] I've sent my lad to the ditch: he'll throw the first bundle.

D32O_TP_01_HIT.en: [delighted] The lad in the fez! The marksman who split Coco's fusta in two on the Horn! [laughs] Then you turned firefighter. [proud] Today you're a gunner again, and the aim is yours.

D32O_TP_GUNNER.en: [shouting] [urgent] A gunner on the wall! While the barrel cools, get behind the gabions!

D32O_TP_NAME_1.en: [curious] Master Urban calls the great gun 'Monday', did you know? Some lad named it. [teasing] Was it you?

D32O_TP_NAME_2.en: [puzzled] Master Urban calls the great gun 'Parcel'. Whatever that means. Some lad named it. [teasing] Was it you?

D32O_TP_NAME_3.en: [amused] Master Urban calls the great gun 'Insurance'; apparently it covers everything. Some lad named it. [teasing] Was it you?

D32O_TP_NAME_4.en: [curious] Master Urban has given the great gun a name, but he won't tell anyone. [probing] Do you know it?
